name: upgrade-migrate-framework-scope
body: source: upgrade/feedback-3 — the migrate half named no concrete migration to plan or test: loadLibraryMeta accepts only `format: 1`, so no older format exists, and the AC "a library at a known older format is migrated in order…" could never be met; "deck migrations run only when provable from the deck's own content" and "a template.yaml schema change" were open-ended with no defined case. Resolution [autonomous]: adopted the coordinator's option (a) — scoped requirements.requirement.upgrade-migrate-format to the migration framework plus the unknown/newer-format refusal and stated explicitly that the registered migration set is empty today (no format older than 1, and a deck has no version field), so adding a migration is a kalide change (registry) and is never inferred from content. The requirement's ACs are now testable today: `format: 1` → no migration, exit 0, byte-for-byte unchanged; `format: 0`/`2` → non-zero, names the format found and the format supported, byte-for-byte untouched; and internal/template.loadLibraryMeta must accept every older format the migrator reads (today exactly `{1}`, so a `format: 1` library loads and a `format: 2` library is refused). Defined "newer than the running kalide" on the format integer, not the version string: the running binary implements the highest `format:` it implements (today 1), and a `dev`/unstamped build implements the same format as its source, so `dev` never means "newer". The deck path is stated as a no-op today (no deck format migration registered) rather than an open-ended content-derived migration. Coherence edits so no node still asserts a content-derived deck migration or an existing older format: requirements.constraint.upgrade-migrations-ordered-atomic, requirements.note.upgrade-deck-vs-library, global.constraint.upgrade-unknown-format-reported, requirements.requirement.deck-library-upgrade, domain.service.upgrade-project.
